skills.name: anomaly-detection-model-builder
skills.title: Anomaly Detection Model Builder
skills.description: Build and evaluate anomaly detection for tabular, sensor and transaction data with few or no labels: define the anomaly type (point, contextual, collective), choose detectors (robust z-score/MAD and IQR rules, Mahalanobis with robust covariance, k-NN distance, LOF, Isolation Forest, one-class SVM, PCA reconstruction / autoencoders, forecasting residuals for time series), combine them by rank, explain each alert by its deviating features, set thresholds from an alert budget or the score distribution, and evaluate with precision@k, PR-AUC and recall on known incidents, or detector agreement when no labels exist. Includes pure-Python detectors (robust z, Mahalanobis, kNN, Isolation Forest, ensemble) and an evaluation script. Use when someone wants to find outliers, unusual transactions, faulty sensors or abnormal behaviour, asks Isolation Forest vs LOF vs one-class SVM, how to set the contamination or threshold, or how to evaluate an anomaly detector.

skills.name: catboost-model-builder
skills.title: CatBoost Model Builder
skills.description: Build CatBoost models that use its strengths correctly: raw categorical columns as cat_features (ordered target statistics, no manual encoding), text_features, Pool construction with NaN-safe categories, ordered boosting and has_time for temporal data, symmetric (oblivious) trees, overfitting detector with eval_set and use_best_model, losses for classification, regression (Quantile, Poisson, Tweedie) and ranking (YetiRank), class weights, monotone constraints, feature importance (PredictionValuesChange, LossFunctionChange) and SHAP values, GPU training and model export. Plans cat/text/numeric columns from a CSV and generates a runnable training script, and checks parameter sets for the conflicts CatBoost rejects (iterations vs n_estimators, Bayesian bootstrap with subsample, multiple class-weight options, depth > 16, use_best_model without eval_set). Use when someone builds or tunes a CatBoost model, has many categorical or high-cardinality features, or hits CatBoostError messages.

skills.name: categorical-encoding-selector
skills.title: Categorical Encoding Selector
skills.description: Choose and implement the right encoding for every categorical column given the model family and the data: one-hot (with infrequent-level grouping and handle_unknown), ordinal with an explicit order, cross-fitted target encoding (scikit-learn TargetEncoder, CatBoost ordered statistics, category_encoders inside CV), frequency/count encoding, feature hashing, native categorical support in LightGBM, HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost and CatBoost, prefix levels for codes (zip3, NAICS-2), and embeddings. Measures cardinality, rare-level share, unseen-level rate on a time-ordered holdout and target signal per column, emits the ColumnTransformer, and quantifies target-encoding leakage (in-sample vs out-of-fold vs holdout AUC). Use when someone asks how to encode categorical variables, one-hot vs target vs ordinal encoding, how to handle high-cardinality IDs, zip codes, unseen categories at inference, or why target encoding overfits.

skills.name: classification-model-selector
skills.title: Classification Model Selector
skills.description: Choose the right classification algorithm for tabular, text or mixed data and prove the choice with a fair bake-off: logistic regression (L2, L1, elastic net), linear SVM, naive Bayes, k-NN, RBF SVM, decision trees, random forest, extra trees, HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, explainable boosting machines (EBM/GAM), points scorecards and MLPs, matched to data size, width, categorical and high-cardinality share, missingness, class imbalance, text, and constraints such as interpretability, monotonic constraints, calibrated probabilities, latency budgets and tiny deployable models. Ranks candidates with starting hyperparameters and cautions, then generates a bake-off script running every candidate on identical CV folds with per-fold metrics, fit time and prediction latency. Use when someone asks which classifier to use, logistic regression vs random forest vs XGBoost, whether deep learning is worth it on tabular data, or wants a model comparison set up.

skills.name: clustering-algorithm-selector
skills.title: Clustering Algorithm Selector
skills.description: Choose the right clustering algorithm and check that clustering makes sense at all: cluster tendency (Hopkins statistic with a correlated-features caveat, nearest-neighbour isolation), then k-means / MiniBatchKMeans, Gaussian mixtures with BIC, agglomerative (Ward, average, complete, single) with dendrograms, DBSCAN, HDBSCAN, OPTICS, spectral clustering, BIRCH, mean shift, k-prototypes and k-modes for mixed or categorical data, and Gower distance, matched to data size, expected shapes, noise, varying density, known k, soft memberships, hierarchy and streaming. Covers preprocessing (scaling, encoding, dimensionality, distance metrics), validation (internal indices, bootstrap stability, external labels, business profiling) and assigning new points. Use when someone wants to segment customers, group products or documents, find natural groups, asks which clustering algorithm to use, k-means vs DBSCAN vs HDBSCAN, or whether their clusters are real.

skills.name: collaborative-filtering-implementer
skills.title: Collaborative Filtering Implementer
skills.description: Implement collaborative filtering recommenders that beat popularity: item-based kNN with cosine, Jaccard or asymmetric similarity, shrinkage, neighbourhood size, positive-only or mean-centred rating signals and 'because you liked X' explanations; implicit ALS with confidence weighting, BPR pairwise ranking and the closed-form EASE model in plain NumPy, tuned on a temporal validation split by recall@k and NDCG@k and refit on all data; plus user-kNN, explicit matrix factorisation, the implicit/LightFM libraries, hyperparameter ranges, cold-start fallbacks, scaling with sparse matrices and approximate nearest neighbours. Produces top-k lists in the format of the recommendation evaluator. Use when someone builds 'users who liked this also liked', item-to-item recommendations, matrix factorisation or ALS/BPR models, or asks why their collaborative filter is no better than recommending bestsellers.

skills.name: counterfactual-explanation-generator
skills.title: Counterfactual Explanation Generator
skills.description: Generate counterfactual explanations and algorithmic recourse: the smallest realistic change to a row's features that changes the model's decision. Solves exact minimal-cost recourse for linear and logistic models (MAD-scaled L1 cost, immutable features, increase/decrease directions, bounds, integer and binary features, diverse alternatives, features every counterfactual must change, and a no-recourse finding when immutable features decide), generates DiCE counterfactuals for any scikit-learn model with constraints turned into permitted ranges and every result re-predicted, and validates counterfactuals from any method for constraint violations, implausible values, off-manifold rows, broken derived-feature relations and failure to flip the prediction. Use when someone asks what a customer or applicant would need to change to get a different outcome, wants counterfactual or what-if explanations, recourse for adverse decisions, or DiCE.

skills.name: cross-validation-strategy-designer
skills.title: Cross-Validation Strategy Designer
skills.description: Design the cross-validation scheme that mirrors how a model will be used, and check the folds before trusting any score: StratifiedKFold and repeated CV for i.i.d. data, GroupKFold / StratifiedGroupKFold / LeaveOneGroupOut when entities repeat (customers, patients, devices, sessions), TimeSeriesSplit with gaps and expanding or sliding windows for forward prediction, purging and embargo for overlapping label windows, nested CV for tuning, spatial and hierarchical grouping, multilabel stratification, small-data choices (repeats, LOO) and the final untouched holdout. Detects repeated-entity and time columns from the data, recommends a splitter with scikit-learn code, and previews or audits folds for group overlap, time-order violations, label-window gaps and missing classes. Use when someone asks how to split data or set up CV, why CV scores are better than production, how to cross-validate time series or grouped data, or wants existing folds checked for leakage.

skills.name: dbscan-parameter-tuner
skills.title: DBSCAN Parameter Tuner
skills.description: Tune DBSCAN (and know when to switch to HDBSCAN or OPTICS): choose min_samples from dimensionality and the smallest meaningful group, find eps from the knee of the k-distance curve with a noise-share bracket, grid-search eps x min_samples for stable regions (cluster count that persists across neighbouring settings, noise share, largest-cluster share, silhouette on non-noise points, ARI against reference labels), and handle scaling, distance metrics (Euclidean, cosine, haversine for coordinates), high dimensions, varying densities, border points, noise interpretation, and assigning new points. Pure-Python k-distance and DBSCAN grid scripts validated against scikit-learn. Use when someone asks how to set eps or min_samples, gets one giant cluster or all-noise results from DBSCAN, clusters geographic points, or needs density-based clustering with outliers.

skills.name: feature-engineering-idea-generator
skills.title: Feature Engineering Idea Generator
skills.description: Generate concrete, leakage-aware feature ideas for tabular ML and the pandas code to build them: infer column roles (IDs, entity keys, datetimes incl. unix epochs, years, amounts, counts, proportions, low- and high-cardinality categoricals, codes like zip, lat/lon, free text), then propose date parts and cyclical encodings, elapsed time to the prediction date, age from year, log1p and clipping for skewed values, missing indicators, rare-level grouping, frequency encoding, code prefixes, text length and TF-IDF, per-unit rates (total / tenure), date differences, geo distances, and point-in-time per-entity aggregates (prior counts, means, time since previous event, velocity). Ranks ideas P1-P3, flags columns that look written after the outcome, and includes domain playbooks (churn, fraud, credit, demand, marketing, real estate, IoT). Use when someone asks for feature ideas, how to improve a model with better features, what features to build from a dataset, or how to encode dates, amounts, IDs or text.

skills.name: feature-importance-reporter
skills.title: Feature Importance Reporter
skills.description: Produce honest feature importance reports by computing several methods on held-out data and explaining where they disagree: impurity/gain importance (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, sklearn MDI), standardised coefficients, permutation importance with repeats and standard deviations, grouped permutation for clusters of correlated features, drop-column importance and mean |SHAP|, all mapped back from encoded columns to input features. Flags features that look important only to impurity measures (split bias, redundancy), features with no measurable held-out effect, identifier-like columns, single features that dominate (leakage), and groups that share information. Use when someone asks which features matter most, needs an importance chart for stakeholders, compares importance methods, or wonders why gain, permutation and SHAP rankings differ.

skills.name: feature-scaling-advisor
skills.title: Feature Scaling Advisor
skills.description: Decide whether and how to scale or transform numeric features for a given model: no scaling for trees and gradient boosting, StandardScaler, RobustScaler for outliers, MinMaxScaler and MaxAbsScaler (sparse data), log1p, Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson PowerTransformer for skew, QuantileTransformer for heavy tails, clipping/winsorising, and target transforms (TransformedTargetRegressor) for skewed regression targets. Measures skew, robust outliers, zeros, negatives and bounds per column, shows how one wide column dominates raw distances, emits a leak-free ColumnTransformer, and measures the effect of each scaling on a k-NN model with cross-validation. Use when someone asks whether to normalise or standardise, which scaler to use, why k-NN / k-means / SVM / PCA / logistic regression behave oddly, how to handle skewed or outlier-heavy features, or whether scaling leaks information.

skills.name: feature-selection-analyzer
skills.title: Feature Selection Analyzer
skills.description: Select features for tabular ML without fooling yourself: filter methods (missingness, near-zero variance, ID-like columns, univariate out-of-fold AUC / Spearman / mutual information, correlation-based redundancy groups keeping the strongest member), embedded methods (L1/elastic net, tree and GBM importance, SelectFromModel), wrapper methods (RFE/RFECV, sequential feature selection, Boruta), permutation importance on held-out data, stability selection across folds and bootstraps, and the cardinal rule that selection happens inside cross-validation. Flags near-perfect single features as probable leaks and measures importance stability across runs. Use when someone asks which features to keep or drop, how to reduce dimensionality before modelling, whether feature importance is trustworthy, why selected features change between folds, or how to avoid selection bias in CV.

skills.name: feature-store-schema-designer
skills.title: Feature Store Schema Designer
skills.description: Design feature store schemas that serve the same features to training and production: entities and join keys, sources with event and created timestamps, feature views grouped by entity and refresh cadence, dtypes, TTLs matched to source cadence, online vs offline stores, freshness SLAs, point-in-time correct historical retrieval, materialisation, feature services per model version, naming conventions with window suffixes, ownership, PII tagging and governance. Lints a JSON/YAML feature spec for 12 design errors and generates a working Feast repository (Entity, FileSource/BigQuerySource/SnowflakeSource/RedshiftSource, FeatureView, FeatureService, feature_store.yaml) verified with feast apply and get_historical_features; maps the design to Tecton, Databricks, SageMaker, Vertex AI and Hopsworks. Use when someone designs or reviews a feature store, asks how to structure feature views, set TTLs, avoid train/serve skew, or turn feature tables into Feast definitions.

skills.name: fraud-detection-model-designer
skills.title: Fraud Detection Model Designer
skills.description: Design fraud detection models that survive production: point-in-time velocity and behaviour features per card, account or device (counts and amounts over sliding windows that exclude the current event, time since previous, amount relative to history, first-time merchant category or country), out-of-time splits with a label-maturity gap for chargeback delay, LightGBM with an Isolation Forest anomaly score, and evaluation the way fraud operations work: average precision against the fraud-rate baseline, precision/recall and value detection rate at alert budgets, recall at fixed false-positive rates, cost-optimal thresholds from fraud losses, review cost and customer friction, alert-capacity constraints and week-by-week stability. Covers rules versus models, label delay and noise, adversarial drift, graph and device signals, real-time scoring and feedback loops. Use when someone builds or reviews a fraud, scam, abuse, chargeback or anti-money-laundering model, sets fraud thresholds, or evaluates a fraud score.

skills.name: hyperparameter-search-planner
skills.title: Hyperparameter Search Planner
skills.description: Plan hyperparameter searches that fit the compute budget and read their results correctly: choose grid, random, successive halving (HalvingRandomSearchCV), Bayesian/TPE (Optuna) or Hyperband/ASHA from fit cost, trial budget, parallel workers and the number of continuous parameters; define search spaces with log scales, conditional parameters and sensible ranges for logistic regression, elastic net, SVM, k-NN, random forest, extra trees, HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost and MLPs; fix what early stopping handles; then analyse cv_results_ or Optuna trials for best configurations, parameters at the edge of their range, sensitivity (including peaked effects), configurations within one standard error, and whether more trials would help. Use when someone asks how to tune a model, grid vs random vs Bayesian search, what ranges to search, how many trials are needed, or how to interpret search results.

skills.name: imbalanced-class-handler
skills.title: Imbalanced Class Handler
skills.description: Handle imbalanced classification (fraud, churn, defaults, failures, rare diseases) without fooling yourself: measure with PR-AUC, recall at capacity and expected cost instead of accuracy, keep test sets at natural prevalence, stratified and repeated CV for few positives, choose thresholds from capacity, costs or precision/recall targets, apply class weights (class_weight, scale_pos_weight, auto_class_weights), resample only inside an imblearn Pipeline (random undersampling, SMOTE, ADASYN, SMOTE-NC, Tomek, ENN), correct probabilities after resampling with the prior-shift formula, calibrate, and know when to switch to anomaly detection or collect more labels. Profiles a dataset's imbalance severity with a cheapest-first strategy ladder and imblearn code, and tunes thresholds under six policies with prior correction. Use when someone has rare positives, asks about SMOTE or class weights, gets high accuracy but useless recall, needs a threshold, or has miscalibrated probabilities after oversampling.

skills.name: kmeans-cluster-count-finder
skills.title: k-Means Cluster Count Finder
skills.description: Choose the number of clusters k for k-means (and k-means-like methods) with evidence instead of a single elbow plot: inertia elbow via the kneedle method, silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz, Davies-Bouldin, the gap statistic against uniform reference data (which also detects that there is no structure at all), bootstrap stability (adjusted Rand index on overlapping subsamples), BIC for Gaussian mixtures, cluster-size floors and business usefulness, then profile the chosen clusters (sizes, standardised feature differences, over-represented categories, outcome by cluster) so they can be named and acted on. Pure-Python k-means++ sweep validated against scikit-learn. Use when someone asks how many clusters to use, gets an ambiguous elbow plot, wants silhouette or gap statistic analysis, or needs to name and sanity-check k-means segments.

skills.name: learning-curve-diagnoser
skills.title: Learning Curve Diagnoser
skills.description: Build and read learning curves (training and validation score versus training-set size) to decide whether a model is data-limited, variance-limited or bias-limited, and therefore whether to collect more data, regularise, add capacity or engineer features. Generates scikit-learn learning_curve scripts with geometric size spacing, seeded shuffling, stratified/grouped/time-ordered splitters, fit times and a plot with std bands, then diagnoses the result: the gap at the largest size, validation gain per doubling, an inverse power-law fit capped at the training score with 2x/4x/10x predictions and the rows needed for a target score, plus warnings for noisy curves, memorisation, and validation that drops as data grows. Use when someone asks whether more data will help, how much data is needed, why validation lags training, or how to read a learning curve plot.

skills.name: learning-to-rank-model-builder
skills.title: Learning-to-Rank Model Builder
skills.description: Build learning-to-rank models for search, recommendations re-ranking and marketplace sorting: validate query-document data (contiguous query groups, single-label and no-relevant queries, duplicates, query-level features, single-feature baselines and leakage-like features), train LightGBM lambdarank and XGBoost rank:ndcg rankers with grouped cross-validation, early stopping on NDCG@k, label gains and truncation, and evaluate per query with NDCG (exponential or linear gain), MAP, MRR, ERR and precision@k, with tie handling made explicit and paired bootstrap / randomisation tests that tell whether a ranker really beats BM25 or the current system. Covers pointwise, pairwise and listwise losses, judgement and click labels, position bias, feature design and online interleaving. Use when someone builds a ranker, re-ranks search results or recommendation candidates, uses LambdaMART, or compares rankings offline.

skills.name: lime-explanation-generator
skills.title: LIME Explanation Generator
skills.description: Generate LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) for tabular predictions that are reproducible and honest: run LimeTabularExplainer with training statistics, categorical encoding decoded inside the prediction function (so Pipelines with one-hot encoders work), quartile rules or continuous slopes, kernel width and sample size chosen deliberately, and repeated runs with different seeds. Then check stability (sign consistency, coefficient of variation, top-k overlap), surrogate fidelity (weighted R^2) and the gap between surrogate and model, and compare signs with SHAP for the same row. Explains when LIME is the right tool, how kernel width and discretisation change the answer, and how to report it. Use when someone asks for LIME explanations, sees LIME give different answers on each run, or needs a model-agnostic local explanation for a black-box model.

skills.name: ml-baseline-model-builder
skills.title: ML Baseline Model Builder
skills.description: Build the baselines every ML model must beat before anyone trusts it: dummy majority/prior/mean/median predictors, the current business rule, a one-feature model (OneR), seasonal-naive and last-value forecasts, popularity recommenders, and a first honest linear model and HistGradientBoosting inside a leak-free scikit-learn Pipeline with a time-ordered, grouped or stratified holdout. Reports ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, log loss, Brier, balanced accuracy, MAE, RMSE, R2 and WAPE side by side, and warns when a first baseline looks too good (leakage). Use when starting a modelling project, asked for a baseline or a quick first model, asked whether a model is actually better than a simple rule, or when results need a reference point for a comparison report.

skills.name: ml-feasibility-assessor
skills.title: ML Feasibility Assessor
skills.description: Decide GO, GO WITH RISKS or NO-GO for an ML project before building it: enough labelled rows and minority examples, events per feature, label quality and coverage, history length and drift, single-feature signal (out-of-fold AUC / Spearman) and suspicious near-perfect predictors, data availability at prediction time, latency and serving constraints, the value ceiling given action capacity, and the cost of being wrong. Includes sample-size arithmetic for metric confidence intervals, AUC standard errors (Hanley-McNeil), McNemar test sizes and data collection time. Use when someone asks whether ML can work for a problem, whether there is enough data, how many labels or positives are needed, whether a dataset has signal, or wants a feasibility review, pilot plan or go/no-go recommendation.

skills.name: ml-model-comparison-reporter
skills.title: ML Model Comparison Reporter
skills.description: Compare machine learning models honestly and write the comparison report: per-fold CV scores analysed with the corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau-Bengio), Wilcoxon signed-rank, Bayesian correlated t-test with a region of practical equivalence, and the Friedman test with average ranks for many models; single-test-set comparisons with the DeLong test for ROC-AUC, McNemar's test on decisions (threshold or top-K), and paired stratified bootstrap CIs for PR-AUC, log loss, Brier, MAE and RMSE; plus practical significance, multiple-comparison control, cost/latency trade-offs and a decision rule. Pure-Python implementations validated against scipy and a brute-force DeLong. Use when someone asks which model is better, whether a gain is significant, how to compare CV results, needs a model comparison table or report for stakeholders, or wants to replace a production model with a challenger.

skills.name: ml-problem-framing-advisor
skills.title: ML Problem Framing Advisor
skills.description: Turn a vague business ask ("use AI to reduce churn", "predict demand", "find fraud") into a precise, buildable ML problem: the decision and action the prediction drives, who acts and with what capacity, the unit and moment of prediction, the label with its observation and outcome windows, label delay, features available at prediction time, task type (binary, multiclass, ordinal, regression, count, forecasting, ranking, anomaly, clustering, uplift), the baseline to beat and the metric at the operating point. Flags leakage-by-framing, proxy labels, feedback loops, selection bias and unactionable predictions. Use when someone asks how to frame an ML problem, what the target should be, whether something is classification or regression, how to define churn or a label window, or wants a framing review before modelling starts.

skills.name: ml-project-scoping-writer
skills.title: ML Project Scoping Writer
skills.description: Write the scoping document (one-pager, PRD section or project charter) for a machine learning project: summary, the decision and its users, success criteria with a primary metric at the operating point, target, baseline, guardrails and online confirmation, data sources with availability at prediction time and the label definition, a phased simplest-first approach, explicit in-scope and out-of-scope lists, milestones with dates and exit criteria, risks with mitigations (leakage, labels, feedback loops, adoption, drift), team and cost, go/no-go kill criteria and open questions. Generates the Markdown from a JSON spec with visible TODOs and lints existing scope docs for missing sections and vague commitments ("leverage AI", "real-time", "state-of-the-art", metrics with no target). Use when someone asks to write, review or tighten an ML project proposal, scope, charter, one-pager or PRD.

skills.name: ml-success-metric-selector
skills.title: ML Success Metric Selector
skills.description: Choose the metric that defines success for an ML model, and the guardrails around it, from the decision it serves: precision/recall@K for capacity-bound actions, expected cost at the cost-optimal threshold for asymmetric errors, PR-AUC vs ROC-AUC for rare events, log loss/Brier/ECE when probabilities are consumed, macro- vs weighted-F1 for multiclass, MAE vs RMSE vs WAPE vs MAPE vs Poisson deviance for regression, MASE/RMSSE and pinball loss for forecasts, NDCG/MRR/recall@k for ranking and recommendation, concordance for survival, Qini/AUUC for uplift. Computes the full metric panel from a predictions CSV (scikit-learn-identical numbers) and finds the cost-minimising threshold. Use when someone asks which metric to use, whether accuracy/AUC/F1/MAPE is right, how to set a threshold from costs, how to turn a business KPI into an offline metric, or wants every metric for a set of predictions.

skills.name: ml-vs-rules-decision-advisor
skills.title: ML vs Rules Decision Advisor
skills.description: Decide whether a problem should be solved with hand-written rules, machine learning, a hybrid of both, or not yet: score twelve factors (labelled data volume, label availability, signal complexity, change rate, rule maintenance pain, scale, error cost, explainability and regulation, latency, team ML maturity, personalisation, feedback speed) with hard gates, learn a shallow readable rule set from a CSV with pure-Python CART and compare its holdout AUC with the ML model, emit the rule as a deployable SQL CASE, and design hybrids (rules as filters, guardrails, model score inside rules, ML-suggested rules). Use when someone asks "do we even need ML?", "rules or a model?", wants to replace a sprawling rule engine, justify an ML project against existing business rules, or plan a migration from rules to ML.

skills.name: model-card-writer
skills.title: Model Card Writer
skills.description: Write model cards that hold up to review: model details, intended and out-of-scope uses, training and evaluation data with periods and label definitions, overall metrics with confidence intervals, the baseline and decision threshold, performance disaggregated by group or segment with bootstrap intervals, fairness gaps (TPR/equal opportunity, FPR, positive rate and the four-fifths ratio), explainability, limitations, ethical considerations, risks with mitigations, and monitoring. Computes slice metrics from a predictions file, generates the card from a JSON spec with visible TODOs for missing sections, and lints existing cards for missing sections, placeholders, metrics without numbers or uncertainty, missing subgroup results and overclaiming language. Follows Mitchell et al. (2019) Model Cards and the Hugging Face card layout. Use when someone documents a model, prepares a model for review or release, or needs a model card, model documentation or a fairness and performance report.

skills.name: optuna-study-writer
skills.title: Optuna Study Writer
skills.description: Write correct, resumable Optuna hyperparameter studies for scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost: an objective with a search space sized to the data, fixed CV folds built once (stratified, grouped or time-ordered), early stopping inside each fold, trial.report and should_prune for MedianPruner / HyperbandPruner, seeded multivariate TPESampler, SQLite storage with study_name and load_if_exists for resuming, stale-study stopping callbacks, user attributes (best iteration, fold std), trials export, parameter importances, conditional spaces, multi-objective studies, and refitting the best configuration with a lower learning rate. Generates verified study scripts for six model families and lints Optuna code: unprunable objectives, inconsistent parameters, per-trial folds, wrong direction, constant-returning handlers, missing seeds or storage, deprecated APIs. Use when someone writes or reviews an Optuna study, wants Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, pruning, or a resumable tuning job.

skills.name: overfitting-underfitting-diagnoser
skills.title: Overfitting / Underfitting Diagnoser
skills.description: Diagnose overfitting and underfitting from the evidence a model leaves behind: training histories (metric per boosting round or epoch from LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Keras or PyTorch) and validation curves (train and validation score across one hyperparameter such as max_depth, C, min_samples_leaf or alpha). Finds the best iteration on a smoothed curve, the overfitting onset, degradation and noise, and suggests early-stopping patience; flags under-training, plateaus, divergence and models that are not learning. For validation curves it labels underfit, sweet-spot and overfit zones, applies the one-standard-error rule to pick the simplest adequate value, infers complexity direction, and warns when the best value sits at the edge of the sweep. skills.name: recast-and-prompt-technique-coach

skills.name: speaking-rubric-builder

skills.name: task-based-language-lesson-designer

skills.name: capa-effectiveness-checker

skills.name: design-of-experiments-planner
